settings.definition: HPZ wheels with a miniature ball bearing in each hub. They roll much farther than plain-axle wheels on a track.
The longer of the two axle lengths, for wide-track castings. Puts the tyre flush with a wide arch instead of tucked inside it.
A decal sheet sealed with clear film at the factory, so the ink will not dissolve in water. No need to spray the sheet before cutting.
Opaque white printing for decals on dark paint. Printed mirrored and applied face-down.
The thin film of excess resin along mould seams. Scrape it off with an upright blade, then sand.
The plug of resin where it entered the mould. Clip it close, then sand flat.
Cyanoacrylate, or super glue. Thin CA wicks into tight joints, medium is for general assembly, gel bridges gaps.
The tyre sits just inside the arch lip, with a small even gap above it. The default clean look.
Wheels that stick out past the fender. Right for a stanced build, wrong on a stock-look car.
Distance across the outside faces of both wheels on one axle. Set by axle length.
The mushroom-headed post that holds a Hot Wheels base to its body. Shave the head, keep the post.
A setting solution that softens decal film so it pulls down over curves and panel lines.
A fine filler primer, usually grey. Shows the defects you missed before colour goes on.
Painting with an almost-dry brush so pigment only catches raised edges. Makes 1:64 metal detail readable.
Very thin dark paint flowed into recesses and wiped off the high points. Adds depth to engines and body lines.
